title: Editorial: Exploring the dynamics of emerging and re-emerging diseases: from origins to impact, volume II
abstract: (2026) conducted a review entitled "One Health innovations in tropical disease surveillance for a resilient future". The study explores current tropical disease surveillance approaches that adopt a "One Health" perspective. They concluded that an effective 'One Health' strategy should be proactive rather than reactive, incorporating climate intelligence and addressing the behavioral and social drivers of disease, while also being supported by multilateral cooperation and policy continuity. The authors emphasized the importance of cross-sectoral integration to improve the early detection and response to disease. Furthermore, they argue that technologies, including artificial intelligence, genomic sequencing, environmental biosensors, and mobile health platforms, are enhancing the speed and scalability of disease detection, response, and the prevention of cross-species transmission. The study also highlighted the critical need for interdisciplinary education, policy support, and real-time data sharing to build system-wide resilience. They recommend involving local communities in ecologically sensitive tropical issues and in formulating context-specific surveillance strategies. Lastly, they argue that embedding 'One Health' principles into surveillance practices transforms reactive systems into resilient ones. (2026) conducted a study entitled "Development and validation of a novel multiplex PCR assay for the detection of Anaplasma, Babesia and Theileria in captive wild ungulates". The researchers developed a multiplex PCR (mPCR) assay to detect Babesia, Theileria and Anaplasma pathogens simultaneously at the genus level in wild ungulates. For piroplasmids (Babesia and Theileria), two pairs of primers were designed using the 18S ribosomal RNA gene. These primers were specific and sensitive and could generate target products of 178 bp for Theileria and 479 bp for Babesia. Additionally, a primer pair targeting the 16S rRNA gene was designed to generate an expected 318 bp product for Anaplasma. These three primer pairs were tested using blood samples collected from 60 captive Gazella bennettii (Family Bovidae) and Axis porcinus (Family Cervidae) from various wildlife parks and zoos in Punjab, Pakistan. The mPCR results produced by these primers were consistent with those from monoplex PCR, with an overall hemoparasites prevalence of 66.66% (40/60). Sequencing of the PCR products confirmed these results, providing a valuable complementary tool for the simultaneous, accurate and routine detection of Anaplasma and piroplasms in endangered wild ungulates. 2026) presented a clinical case report entitled "Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease following venison exposure in a chronic wasting disease-endemic region: a zoonotic surveillance perspective". This study involved a thorough evaluation of the clinical progression, diagnostic assessment, and public health investigation of a patient with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), which is a fatal condition caused by prions. The results they published showed that the 72year-old hunter developed progressive rapid dementia and startle myoclonus. During hospitalization, the patient developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Magnetic resonance imaging showed cortical ribboning and diffusion restriction in the basal ganglia, while cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers (RT-QuIC, total tau and 14-3-3) and post-mortem neuropathology confirmed sporadic CJD of the MM1 subtype. The public health implications of the disease were discussed at length, particularly regarding hunters with extensive exposure to cervids. 2026) conducted a study in Qinghai Province, China titled "Mpox-HIV coinfection in a low-incidence setting: epidemiological insights from Qinghai, China". The study examined the epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of mpox-HIV coinfection in a male patient who had sex with men, as well as systemic gaps in surveillance, diagnosis, and the response to the infection. The patient presented with a fever of 39.4°C and the recovery of mpox virus (MPXV) nucleic acid was confirmed following the collection of a nasopharyngeal swab specimen. Further characterization and identification of the virus revealed it to be MPXV clade IIb (formerly known as the West African clade), C.1.1 sub lineage, with the full designation B.1.3.1.1. As the authors suggest, the findings of this study indicate that the most likely route of exposure for the patient was high-risk sexual contact within a social or sexual network, since no history of international travel was recorded. This finding suggests that silent transmission may already be occurring in regions with low incidence. 2026) conducted a study on the rates of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection and its relationship with vaccination status. They retrospectively analyzed data from patients who experienced reinfection during the second and third waves of the pandemic. Of the 458 participants in the study, 62 (13.54%) who had a primary infection were confirmed to have had a reinfection. Furthermore, 60 participants (13%) were asymptomatic, while 398 participants (87%) were symptomatic, with fever being the most frequently observed symptom during both primary (70.3%) and reinfection (72.58%) infections. Lastly, an association was observed between infection status and vomiting symptoms, which was statistically significant (p < 0.01).Carrero and Mosquera's (2026) article was a review of the re-emergence of arboviruses in the Andean-Amazonian corridor in Latin America. Datasets on various vector-borne diseases from selected countries were analyze from 2023 to 2026 to comprehend epidemiological trends of reemerging diseases. The results showed persistence of malaria in Amazonian areas as well as a sustained increase in arboviruses infection such as yellow fever, dengue and chikungunya. For instance, 132 confirmed human cases of yellow fever outbreak was recorded in Colombia from 2024 to 2025 while 65 death was registered in Ecuador from 37,840 cases of dengue. Furthermore, signs of reemergence of yellow fever were observed in Venezuela during 2025 and 2026 which was attributed to the sylvatic cycles of the virus. The study revealed that the re-emergence of some arboviruses is linked to ecological, social and health factors, as well as poor health education, vaccine hesitancy, limited access to health services, the infodemic and weaknesses in epidemiological surveillance and vector control. In conclusion, the Research Topic has explored the complex and multifaceted aspects of emerging and re-emerging of vector-borne diseases. Also, this topic has provided deeper understanding of the ecological, genetic, environmental and socioeconomic factors that drive the emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases while exploring their cascading effects on public health, societies, and economies.

title: TAPPR PCR Assay Design – Targeted, Automated, Primer and Probe Retrieval for Scalable Molecular Assay Design
abstract: Abstract Motivation The rapid and reliable detection of infectious disease agents is critical for effective biosurveillance, diagnostics, and outbreak response. However, existing molecular assay design methods face significant limitations in scalability, speed, and adaptability to rapidly evolving pathogens, often leading to outdated or suboptimal assays. Here, we present Targeted, Automated Primer and Probe Retrieval (TAPPR), a novel, automated pipeline for scalable molecular assay design. TAPPR employs alignment-free methods to identify conserved regions and marker sequences across large-scale genomic datasets, supporting customizable design parameters for inclusivity, exclusivity, and assay specificity. To evaluate TAPPR's performance, assays were designed for diverse microbial targets, including Mpox, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, SARS-CoV-2, and Candida albicans, representing viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens. The pipeline incorporates k-mer set operations and clustering strategies to address sequence diversity and streamline conserved region identification. Designed assays underwent in silico PCR simulations and laboratory testing to assess specificity, sensitivity, and exclusivity. Results demonstrated high accuracy across targets, with superior sensitivity to existing fielded assays where available. Additionally, we compare TAPPR to alternative available molecular assay design tools to demonstrate its advantages. source_records.title: TAPPR PCR Assay Design – Targeted, Automated, Primer and Probe Retrieval for Scalable Molecular Assay Design
source_records.abstract: Abstract Motivation The rapid and reliable detection of infectious disease agents is critical for effective biosurveillance, diagnostics, and outbreak response. However, existing molecular assay design methods face significant limitations in scalability, speed, and adaptability to rapidly evolving pathogens, often leading to outdated or suboptimal assays. Here, we present Targeted, Automated Primer and Probe Retrieval (TAPPR), a novel, automated pipeline for scalable molecular assay design. TAPPR employs alignment-free methods to identify conserved regions and marker sequences across large-scale genomic datasets, supporting customizable design parameters for inclusivity, exclusivity, and assay specificity. To evaluate TAPPR's performance, assays were designed for diverse microbial targets, including Mpox, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, SARS-CoV-2, and Candida albicans, representing viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens. The pipeline incorporates k-mer set operations and clustering strategies to address sequence diversity and streamline conserved region identification. Designed assays underwent in silico PCR simulations and laboratory testing to assess specificity, sensitivity, and exclusivity. Results demonstrated high accuracy across targets, with superior sensitivity to existing fielded assays where available. Additionally, we compare TAPPR to alternative available molecular assay design tools to demonstrate its advantages. This work highlights TAPPR’s capability to accelerate the development of molecular diagnostics by efficiently leveraging vast genomic datasets and addressing computational bottlenecks. title: Controlling the Transmission Dynamics of Monkey Pox Infection: A Mathematical Model Approach
abstract: The spread of Monkey Pox (Mpox) poses significant public health challenges, requiring effective intervention strategies to mitigate its impact. This study propose a mathematical model to explore the transmission dynamics of Mpox and assess the impact of quarantine as a control measure. The model divides the population into compartments representing Susceptible, Exposed, Infectious, Quarantined, and Recovered individuals. The system of ordinary differential equations describing the dynamics of the infection were derived. The equilibrium states of the model equations: Disease free equilibrium and Disease endemic equilibrium states were obtained. The stability analysis of the disease free equilibrium was analyzed and found it to be stable. The reproduction number ( R 0 ) was obtained and its numerical value was computed. Numerical simulations were performed to investigate how varying quarantine rates affect the progression of the disease across these compartments. The simulations explore the implications of different quarantine intensities on the number of infectious and exposed individuals over time. The results obtained indicate that quarantine can effectively reduce the transmission rate of the infection. Also, it revealed the potential of quarantine to reduce the disease spread and alleviate its overall impact on the population. The findings offered a framework for understanding the dynamics of Mpox transmission and assist public health authorities in designing effective intervention strategies.

title: Pietro Verri: The History of Smallpox Vaccination Through His Pencil
abstract: ABSTRACT The last case of natural smallpox infection occurred in 1977, and the disease is considered eradicated since 1980. Throughout the history of medicine, early attempts to combat smallpox involved inoculation, a practice based on the observation that those who recovered from the disease became immune. The Lombard Enlightenment movement marked a period of intellectual flourishing in the 18th century, during which reason, science, and progress took center stage. Pietro Verri, a prominent intellectual, was a key figure in this movement on the Italian peninsula. Interestingly, he was deeply fascinated by medicine and what we now refer to as public health. His style was characterized by clarity, logic, and a profound understanding of human behavior. His writings are still influential today and could shed light on the history of variolation and smallpox vaccination. Pietro Verri practiced a form of proto‐vaccination on his daughter even before Edward Jenner's experiment on his young son in 1790. Verri's figure could serve as an example of the promotion of vaccination both on a scientific and public level during an era characterized by a hesitant attitude towards such a practice.

title: Structural transition of the immature poxvirus scaffold from preassembly to the scaffold lattice
abstract: During poxvirus morphogenesis, the external scaffold defines the shape and size of immature virions. However, its structural characterization has been hindered by the pleomorphic nature of authentic virus particles. Here, we present single-particle cryo-electron microscopy and cryo-electron tomography structures of two distinct in vitro assemblies of the vaccinia virus scaffold protein D13 that recapitulate oligomeric states previously observed in situ. These structures reveal a dramatic transition from rod-like oligomers, representing a pre-assembly state, to a fully formed scaffold, triggered by the docking of the N-terminal peptide of the viral membrane protein A17 into the base cavity of D13. We propose that this interaction destabilizes the pre-assembly conformation and initiates scaffold formation upon viral membrane recruitment, ultimately leading to the formation of immature virions. Our findings provide structural insights into the early stages of poxvirus morphogenesis and establish a mechanistic link between conformational changes in D13 and scaffold assembly. Scaffold protein governs the morphology of immature poxvirus particles. Here the authors report cryo-electron microscopy structures of in vitro assemblies and demonstrate a transition from a preassembly state to a fully assembled scaffold upon structural reorganization.

The review includes a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding in meta-analyses and discusses the use of E-values for quantifying the potential importance of residual confounding.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that vaccination against mpox is effective, with no major areas of disagreement. The pooled estimate suggests a significant reduction in mpox incidence among vaccinated individuals.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There are controversies regarding the potential for unmeasured confounding, and the review highlights the need for sensitivity analysis to address this issue. The review also notes the importance of using E-values to quantify the potential impact of unmeasured confounding.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Specific priorities for research include further investigation into the effectiveness of vaccines in different populations and the development of strategies to mitigate the potential impact of unmeasured confounding.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述专注于疫苗用于猴痘的母体和儿科使用,特别关注安全性和有效性。核心问题是评估疫苗在这些人群中的使用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一项活的系统评价和荟萃分析,未明确提及数据库、搜索日期或纳入标准。该综述包括未测量混杂因素的敏感性分析,并讨论了使用E值量化残留混杂因素潜在影响的方法。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,疫苗接种对抗猴痘是有效的,没有重大分歧。汇总估计表明,接种疫苗个体中猴痘 发病率的发病率显著降低。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于未测量混杂因素的潜在影响存在争议,综述强调需要进行敏感性分析以解决这一问题。综述还指出,使用E值量化未测量混杂因素潜在影响的重要性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究的具体优先事项包括进一步调查疫苗在不同人群中的有效性以及开发减轻未测量混杂因素潜在影响的策略。

title: Analysis of Mpox intervention measures in presence of environmental transmission pathway using data from DRC
abstract: This paper develops a mathematical model for Mpox transmission dynamics accounting for disease transmission through interpersonal contact as well as from microbes infested environment. The endemic equilibrium of the model was evaluated for two cases. (1) When it is assumed that the microbes in the environment play no role in the spread of the disease, and it was shown that the endemic equilibrium is unique, exists when R 0 is greater than unity, and is globally asymptotically stable. (2) For the case when environmental microbes concentration plays a role in disease transmission, the model was shown to possibly exhibit backward bifurcation at R 0 . This indicates that lowering R 0 below 1 may not eliminate Mpox when the disease is already endemic, due to the stable endemic equilibrium. Numerical results, based on outbreak data from the DRC indicate that; (1) increased interpersonal contact has the potential of making the disease worse, (2) high isolation rate and accelerated recovery of infected individuals through any possible intervention can easily contain the disease. The results further show that environmental contamination does not substantially influence disease transmission rates. More still, it is observed that implementation of influential mitigation measures results in lower and delayed peaks of the number of infected. This is essential for healthcare systems to prepare for more emergency cases and isolation facilities when needed most especially in under resourced communities or countries. Our findings highlight the need for comprehensive interventions addressing both behavioural and environmental factors, especially in environments with limited resources.

full_text: Salt iodisation gap harmed children’s health and education in Ethiopia The interruption of Ethiopia’s iodised salt supply in 1998 had lasting consequences for children’s survival and academic achievement, according to a study in Nature Food.1 Ethiopia banned the sale on non-iodised salt in 1996, achieving high coverage through supplies imported mainly from neighbouring Eritrea. The border conflict that began in May 1998 halted these imports, sharply reducing household access to iodised salt. Researchers from Ethiopia, the United States and the United Kingdom compared national secondary school examination results for more than 1 million children born in the three years before and after the disruption. They used demographic and health survey data to assess child survival, and soil and crop data to examine geographical differences in naturally occurring iodine. Children exposed to iodine deficiency before birth or during early childhood achieved lower secondary school and university entrance examination scores. Childhood mortality also increased. The effects were greatest in rural areas with low environmental iodine, where locally produced food provided little protection against the loss of iodised salt. Mandatory salt iodisation was reintroduced in Ethiopia in 2012. The researchers say the findings demonstrate the importance of resilient fortification programmes, and the long-term health and educational benefits of preventing iodine deficiency. Portable mpox test performs well in Uganda A portable molecular test for mpox produced results in under 40 minutes and showed high diagnostic accuracy during a field evaluation in Uganda, according to a study in The Lancet Infectious Diseases.2 The Dragonfly OPXV/MPXV platform was tested at six health facilities in Kampala and Wakiso between September and November 2025. Researchers enrolled about 300 people with suspected mpox and tested samples from skin lesions at the point of care. The results were compared with those from real-time quantitative PCR, which requires specialised laboratory infrastructure and is generally conducted at a central laboratory. Dragonfly’s results showed 98.7% overall agreement with PCR testing. For monkeypox virus, the platform achieved a sensitivity of 98.5% and specificity of 96.2%. Frontline health workers reported high acceptability and valued the platform’s ability to avoid centralised laboratory logistics, although they identified training and reliable supply chains as requirements for routine use. Developed at Imperial College London, Dragonfly is currently only used for research purposes. The authors say it could support faster diagnosis in high-burden, resource-limited settings. Further studies are needed to assess its cost-effectiveness, integration into existing diagnostic systems and performance across virus clades and population groups. New model estimates Mediterranean earthquake risk Tunisian researchers have developed a hybrid statistical model to estimate the probability that seismic activity will exceed a specified magnitude within a particular period. The framework, described in the Journal of Earth System Science,3 combines conventional computing, artificial intelligence and quantum-inspired techniques. It uses Bernoulli-based binary classification to estimate the probability that seismic activity will exceed a defined magnitude threshold, rather than attempting to predict an earthquake’s precise magnitude. The researchers applied the model to earthquake data from Algeria, Greece, Italy and Turkey. It performed best on the Greek dataset, where it achieved a hit rate of 71%. The Mediterranean is one of the world’s most seismically active regions, owing to interactions between the African, Eurasian and Arabian tectonic plates. The researchers say probabilistic models could strengthen regional risk assessment and preparedness, although further evaluation would be needed before the approach could contribute to operational early warning systems. Salmonella vaccine may need public funding to attract investment A proposed vaccine protecting children against typhoid and invasive non-typical Salmonella could attract substantial demand in sub-Saharan Africa, but may offer insufficient commercial returns without support from global health funders. Researchers developed a model to forecast demand, revenue and return on investment for a hypothetical trivalent vaccine, according to a study in npj Vaccines.4 The model covered the costs of vaccine development, licensing and manufacturing. By the twelfth year after introduction, annual demand could reach 47 million doses for a one-dose regimen, and 96 million doses for a two-dose regimen. These volumes could generate annual revenues of US$94 million and US$191 million respectively. Despite the potential demand, the projected returns might not be sufficient to attract pharmaceutical investment under several scenarios modelled. The authors say public and philanthropic funding, risk-sharing arrangements and other financing mechanisms may therefore be needed to support the vaccine’s development and commercial viability.

Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Dispatch Monkeypox Virus in Healthcare Settings, Sierra Leone, June 2025 Suggested citation for this article Abstract During the 2025 mpox outbreak in Sierra Leone, we assessed environmental contamination in 2 hospitals. Of 89 surfaces sampled, 6 (6.7%) surface samples, primarily from doors, were PCR-positive for monkeypox virus. Our findings highlight monkeypox virus surface contamination in healthcare settings and help prioritize infection prevention and control targets in resource-limited settings. Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), is a zoonotic disease historically endemic to Central and West Africa (1). Since 2022, the global spread of MPXV clade IIb has altered transmission dynamics, and reports of sustained human-to-human transmission have increased (2,3). Environmental contamination by MPXV has been identified, including recovery of infectious virus particles in healthcare facilities where infection prevention and control (IPC) resources might be limited (4,5). Beginning in January 2025, Sierra Leone experienced a substantial mpox outbreak, representing one of the country’s largest recorded clusters, which strained public health resources. Data on environmental contamination in healthcare settings in Africa during active mpox outbreaks remain scarce. We conducted surface sampling in 2 major urban hospitals in Sierra Leone to assess the presence of MPXV and identify high-risk contamination sites to inform local IPC strategies. The study was conducted in June 2025 at Connaught Hospital in Freetown, the capital and largest city of Sierra Leone, and Bo Government Hospital in Bo, Sierra Leone. Both facilities are referral centers currently managing suspected and confirmed mpox cases during the national mpox outbreak. We sampled 89 high-touch surfaces in clinical and nonclinical areas, including patient beds, door handles, bathroom fixtures such as toilet seats and faucet taps, and nonsingle-use medical equipment such as medical instrument trays and blood pressure cuffs that are supposed to be sterilized after every use. We swabbed each surface for ≈3 minutes by using a polyester-tipped applicator premoistened with viral transport media, by following a standardized protocol (6). We standardized surface area swabbing by using a template. Our sampling did not target specific rooms with known mpox patients and was conducted without interfering with routine cleaning schedules, to reflect typical environmental conditions. The study was approved by the Sierra Leone Ethics and Scientific Review Committee (protocol no. 010/05/2025) and the University of Manitoba Health Research Ethics Board. We extracted DNA by using KingFisher Flex (Thermo Fisher Scientific, https://www.thermofisher.com), a robotic magnetic bead–based system. We performed real-time PCR targeting the MPXV B6R gene by using published primers and probe sequences (7). The 40-cycle assay included negative and positive controls. We set thermal cycling conditions to 95°C for 2 minutes, followed by 40 cycles of 95°C for 15 seconds, and 60°C for 1 minute. We established a positive cycle threshold (Ct) cutoff of <38 on the basis of other environmental MPXV studies (8). Of the 89 surfaces sampled, 6 (6.7%) surface samples were PCR-positive for MPXV. Positivity was 4.0% in Freetown (2 positive of 50 tested) and 10.3% in Bo (4 positive of 39 tested); this difference might reflect variation in IPC practices or frequency of mpox patient contact with sampled surfaces. Ct values for positive samples ranged from 32.34–37.91 (Appendix Table), indicating a range of viral load. A total of 28 doors were sampled and accounted for 2 (33.3%) of the 6 positive surfaces. Other positive surfaces included a delivery bed and weighing scale, a medical ward instrument tray, a laboratory, an office bathroom, and an eye clinic table (Appendix Table). The concentration of MPXV DNA on doors and other high-touch points aligns with fomite transmission risks identified in similar investigations (9). Although Ct values are not a direct proxy for infectivity, lower Ct values (<30) might indicate a higher likelihood of viable virus (8). The positive Ct values we observed suggest moderate viral DNA load on those surfaces, likely below the threshold for recovering infectious viruses. Other studies report similar findings, in which Ct values ranged from 22–38 on high-touch objects in healthcare and residential settings (10,11). We detected MPXV DNA on 6.7% of sampled high-touch surfaces in 2 hospitals in Sierra Leone during the 2025 national mpox outbreak. Doors were the most contaminated surface type, consistent with studies from other settings and highlighting their role as critical fomites requiring targeted disinfection (10,12). The Ct values observed from positive samples (mostly >32) indicate the presence of MPXV DNA, but do not suggest infectivity. However, we did not perform viability studies. Although culture-based studies suggest a viable virus is less likely at Ct values >30, the detection of the MPXV DNA on high-contact surfaces underscores their potential as a reservoir for transmission in the absence of consistent, low, or proper IPC practices (13). Our study suggests that doors and other high-touch surfaces within healthcare clinics assessed are highly susceptible surfaces for MPXV contamination. This could reflect the large number of patients entering and leaving various rooms within the healthcare facility and the low frequency or improper practice of IPC within the hospital. Limitations of our study include the cross-sectional design and purposive sampling of specific high-touch surfaces, which limits generalizability, and a lack of data on cleaning frequency or direct links to nosocomial transmission events. Furthermore, the epidemiologic context of the 2025 mpox outbreak in Sierra Leone, with high community transmission, likely influenced the background level of environmental contamination within healthcare facilities. Despite those limitations, detection of MPXV DNA on high-touch surfaces in a resource-constrained setting reinforces the necessity of robust IPC measures and considerations. The 2025 mpox outbreak in Sierra Leone underscores the ongoing threat of mpox in West Africa and the strain on health systems. Strengthened environmental hygiene, focused and frequent disinfection of high-touch surfaces such as doors and bed rails, and adherence to hand hygiene, are necessary to reduce surface contaminations in healthcare settings (14). Integrating simple, periodic environmental surveillance into outbreak response might help identify IPC gaps, guide resource allocation, and tailor staff training in similar low-resource settings (15). Ms. Jaba is an MSc student in the Department of Medical Microbiology & Infectious Diseases, Rady Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, MB, Canada, and is originally from Sierra Leone. Her research interests focus on virologic and epidemiologic characteristics of emerging zoonotic viruses. Acknowledgments The authors acknowledge the staff at the Bo Government and Connaught hospitals for providing access for sample collection in various locations around the hospitals during these challenging times. The authors also acknowledge the support provided by the Molecular Pathogenesis laboratory at the Department of Biological Sciences, Njala University, Njala Campus in Makonde, for all sample processing and analysis. This work was supported by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research, the International Mpox Research Consortium, and the Department of Defense Threat Reduction Agency. I.I.B. consults to the Weapons Threat Reduction Program at Global Affairs Canada. This manuscript was preprinted at https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.09.16.25335757.
